issue.title: Audit non-TUI callers of read_artifact_file_index for the same per-call re-parse pattern
issue.description:
Proposed by phase bead sase-l6.6 (land phase of epic sase-l6, SASE CONTEXT incremental enrichment); named as follow-up 5 in plans:202608/sase_context_incremental.md.

Epic sase-l6 phase sase-l6.2 added a process-wide revalidating snapshot cache inside read_artifact_file_index() (src/sase/core/artifact_file_explicit.py), scoped to fix the TUI's per-agent-selection re-parse cost. Callers outside the TUI now inherit that cache automatically (same module-level cache), which is a free win, but they were not individually audited for their own per-call re-parse patterns or usage shape:

  src/sase/artifact_cli/prune.py:68            (CLI, one-shot -- likely fine as-is)
  src/sase/axe/run_agent_exec_finalize_artifacts.py:250  (per-agent-run finalization -- may call
                                                            this once per finalize; worth checking
                                                            whether that is now effectively free or
                                                            still a bottleneck at scale)
  src/sase/core/artifact_file_reclaim.py:164
  src/sase/core/artifact_file_facade.py (re-exports read_artifact_file_index and
                                          list_indexed_artifact_files publicly)

Scope: confirm each of these callers benefits from (or at least is not harmed by) the new snapshot cache, and check whether any of them have a same-process, high-frequency call pattern (e.g. batch finalization of many agents) that would benefit from the same treatment the TUI got, now that a cache exists to lean on.
